title: Gadoxetic acid in China: a narrative review of the 15-year journey and the road ahead

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Gadoxetic acid in China: a narrative review of the 15-year journey and the road ahead》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background and objective · abstract-1-1】Since its pivotal introduction in 2011, gadoxetic acid has fundamentally revolutionized the landscape of hepatobiliary imaging in China, shifting the diagnostic paradigm from morphological assessment toward functional hepatocyte-level evaluation. This review comprehensively summarizes its 15-year clinical evolution within the Chinese healthcare system, exploring its pharmacological benefits, advanced applications, and future integration with data-driven frameworks.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Gadoxetic acid in China: a narrative review of the 15-year journey and the road ahead》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】A systematic literature search was conducted across major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, spanning from 2011 to 2026. The search targeted peer-reviewed articles, consensus statements, clinical guidelines, and high-impact reviews published in English and Chinese regarding gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

【Key content and findings · abstract-3-1】Gadoxetic acid provides high sensitivity for early small hepatocellular carcinoma (sHCC) detection via specific OATP1B3 uptake. Beyond lesion detection, its quantitative mapping shows potential for estimating hepatic functional reserve (HFR) and risk stratification for post-hepatectomy liver failure. Crucially, the ongoing paradigm shift toward integrating radiomics and deep learning bridges macroscopic imaging and microscopic molecular biology, theoretically enabling a multi-dimensional profile of liver parenchyma and lesions within a single diagnostic session. However, a significant gap remains between retrospective predictive performance and clinical readiness, and these data-driven frameworks currently serve as supplementary investigational engines rather than standalone clinical decision-makers. Moving forward, integrating these high-dimensional signatures into constructs such as "digital twin" represents the next frontier. Furthermore, China's hepatitis B virus-dominant epidemiological cohorts, comprehensive multi-modal datasets, "Med-Engineering" fusion, and collaborative networks uniquely accelerate the development and preliminary validation of these models, offering valuable insights for global precision hepatology within China's healthcare system.
